title: GitHub Trending Summary - Daily - 2026-10-08
ranking_basis: GitHub Trending daily star gains, sorted descending
ranking_explanation: Daily star-gain figures were read from GitHub Trending and entries reordered by that figure. Total stars, primary language, and default-branch commit were corroborated through the GitHub REST API.
global_caveat: This is a point-in-time snapshot. Daily gains can change as GitHub refreshes the page; daily Trending is not a stable historical record.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Agent-oriented developer tooling dominates today's snapshot: reverse-engineering with agents is the clear leader, while reusable agent skills and workflow utilities also draw strong attention. A PS5 executable-porting project is a notable non-agent outlier.

sections.title: morluto/rea
sections.description: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.
sections.why_notable: The largest daily gain by a wide margin; its README describes one investigation interface spanning application behavior and native binaries.

sections.title: boykopovar/AnyPS5
sections.description: Tool for automatic PS5 executables porting to Linux and Windows.
sections.why_notable: A strong non-agent spike; the project describes relinking executables and implementing system libraries rather than relying on a separate emulation runtime.

sections.title: DuarteSantos8/openGym
sections.description: Self-hosted gym & body-weight tracker — plan routines, log workouts (supersets, warm-ups, cardio), see which muscles are trained, fatigued or detrained, import from FitNotes/Strong/Hevy, passkey login. Your data, your server.
sections.why_notable: A fast-rising personal-data app stands out among the otherwise agent-heavy list.

sections.title: mattpocock/skills
sections.description: Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory.
sections.why_notable: Its unusually large existing audience and strong daily gain underline demand for reusable, engineer-controlled agent workflows.

sections.title: tester-army/e2e
sections.description: Next generation e2e testing framework for web and mobile apps.
sections.why_notable: Testing infrastructure is a substantial secondary theme alongside agents.

sections.title: cathrynlavery/diagram-design
sections.description: Editorial diagram design for Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Factory Droid, and Pi. 42 diagram types. Self-contained HTML + SVG. No shadows. No Mermaid slop.
sections.why_notable: It brings a design-quality and documentation angle to agent skills, with static output as the default.

sections.title: addyosmani/agent-skills
sections.description: Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents.
sections.why_notable: Reinforces the rise of portable, task-specific agent capabilities.

sections.title: ayghri/i-have-adhd
sections.description: A skill to stop your coding agent from burying the answer. ADHD-friendly output.
sections.why_notable: A user-experience-oriented skill is gaining traction alongside engineering-focused agent packages.

sections.title: thedotmack/claude-mem
sections.description: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent – Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode + More
sections.why_notable: Persistent memory is a distinct infrastructure layer for multi-session agent workflows.

sections.title: cloudflare/security-audit-skill
sections.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings
sections.why_notable: It applies agents to a high-stakes engineering task and emphasizes independently verified results.

sections.title: trycua/cua
sections.description: Scale computer-use 2.0 with open-source drivers, cross-OS fleets, and benchmarks for training, evaluation, and data generation.
sections.why_notable: Computer interaction remains a smaller but visible agent-adjacent infrastructure theme.

sections.title: EpicGames/raddebugger
sections.description: A native, user-mode, multi-process, graphical debugger.
sections.why_notable: A traditional systems-development tool provides a counterpoint to the agent-skills cluster.

sections.title: manaflow-ai/cmux
sections.description: Open source Ghostty-based macOS terminal with vertical tabs and notifications for AI coding agents. Built for multitasking, organization, and programmability.
sections.why_notable: It represents interface and workspace tooling built around concurrent coding-agent use.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Coding-agent skills and workflows: mattpocock/skills, addyosmani/agent-skills, ayghri/i-have-adhd, cathrynlavery/diagram-design, and cloudflare/security-audit-skill show packaging of agent behavior into reusable task-specific instructions. Agent infrastructure and interaction: morluto/rea connects agents to reverse-engineering tools; thedotmack/claude-mem addresses persistent context; trycua/cua targets computer-use drivers and evaluation; manaflow-ai/cmux focuses on the agent workspace. Non-agent standouts include boykopovar/AnyPS5 and DuarteSantos8/openGym; tester-army/e2e and EpicGames/raddebugger represent testing and debugging. TypeScript (3) and JavaScript (3) are most common among these 13 entries; C++, Shell, HTML, Python, C, Rust, and Swift each appear once. Counts reflect GitHub's primary-language labels for this list, not overall GitHub usage.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's strongest signal is not simply “more AI”: it is a move toward modular agent workflows, with reusable skills, persistent context, specialist tool access, and dedicated interfaces. Still, the top list includes substantial momentum in testing, gaming compatibility, and personal self-hosted software, so the day's activity is broader than agent tooling alone.
